content:
The Malta Memorial is a commemorative war memorial monument located in Floriana, Malta. It commemorates over 2,298 Commonwealth aircrew who lost their lives during World War II around the Mediterranean theatre and who have no known grave.

When significant numbers of fallen service personnel cannot be linked to a known grave, the Commonwealth War Graves Commission (CWGC) traditionally erects a memorial to honor them. The CWGC built the Malta Memorial for airmen in this position and the monument was unveiled on 3 May 1954.

The monument is designed by Sir Hubert Worthington and represents a golden eagle, a symbol frequently associated with air forces, on top of a limestone pillar, soaring above the waves of the ocean. The monument is roughly 15 feet high, the eagle has a wingspan of about 13 feet, and it is constructed out of bronze. 

Situated in the area of the capital Valletta, the monument is surrounded by a well-preserved garden which offers excellent open views of the harbor and the city. 

The names of the 2,298 fallen airmen are engraved on two large stone plaques at the base of the monument, along with information about the relevant Commonwealth country and their rank. The motto of the monument is "Their Name Liveth For Evermore".

The people commemorated by the Malta Memorial came from all parts of the Commonwealth, with the majority from UK and include people not only from aircrew forces but also paratroopers and glider troops.
